headline: Planning a Kitchen Appliance Layout: What to Confirm Before Ordering Cabinets
articleBody:
When you remodel a kitchen, setting up your appliance layout involves much more than picking attractive finishes. A working kitchen requires clear circulation paths and practical landing areas that match how you actually cook. Before committing to cabinet orders or framing changes, verify that your plan leaves sufficient space for everyday tasks.

What Can Change the Right Choice
The overall room footprint and existing structural walls dictate how smoothly your zones connect. Industry standards suggest maintaining at least 30 by 48 inches of clear floor area in front of every major appliance to prevent bottlenecks. If you place a cooktop along a counter run, balance it with dedicated landing space—ideally 12 inches on one side and 15 inches on the other—so hot cookware never ends up in a walkway.

Work zones also depend heavily on traffic patterns. An open dishwasher door requires at least 21 inches of standing clearance beside it so you can comfortably unload dishes without being pinned against an island. Similarly, buying a French-door refrigerator without checking the surrounding wall depth can keep the doors from swinging past ninety degrees, blocking interior drawers.

When Professional Guidance Helps
If you are moving walls, adding an island, or shifting utility rough-ins across the room, working with a general contractor ensures your layout aligns with real-world dimensions.
